text:
dave_customer: Hey, heads up — since ~09:00 UTC our traffic that should be pinned to eu-west is landing in us-west. App latency jumped from ~80ms to 800-1200ms and we started seeing 401 billing errors. We haven't changed client config. Any ideas?

alice_support: Sorry about that — can you paste the failover policy you have configured (JSON/YAML) and the API key you're using (redact key)?

dave_customer: Here's the policy we use (redacted):
```yaml
failover_policy:
  primary: eu-west-1
  fallback: us-west-2
  sticky_session: true
  sticky_ttl_sec: 60
  weights: [100, 0]
  priority_order: [0, 1]
```
We set sticky_ttl to 60s to keep sessions in eu for short bursts.

bob_prodeng: quick note — we rolled a config parser tweak in last night's deploy that changes how "priority_order" is interpreted if weights present. Could be related. cc @eve_infra

carol_sre: Two quick repro attempts: 1) If the session cookie expires, requests will fallback per priority/weight — which is expected. 2) But I'm seeing a path where a missing weight or malformed array causes an implicit priority inversion. Need logs.

dave_customer: We didn't change TTL or cookies. We see many 401s in logs with x-region:us-west-2 and x-auth-check:failed. Our client sets region in header: X-Region: eu-west-1.

alice_support: Thanks — can you run this curl to reproduce and paste response headers?
curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer [REDACTED]' -H 'X-Region: eu-west-1' https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/generate

(If you get 401 + x-region:us-west-2 we can chase routing path.)

dave_customer: Ran it, got 401. Response headers: 
```
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
x-region: us-west-2
x-routing-reason: failover-apply (sticky-ttl-expired || priority-mismatch)
x-failover-config-version: 2026-03-15-rc2
```

eve_infra: That x-routing-reason string is diagnostic — helpful. I'm pulling the decision trace for that API key now. Initial look: sticky cookie was issued, but subsequent request used a different session token and the parser dropped weights array due to trailing comma in the YAML when we compiled config; compiled policy ended up with priority_order reversed.

bob_prodeng: Yup that matches the parser tweak note. If weights array parsing fails we currently fall back to interpreting priority as index positions, which flips the effective order in some cases. Not intended.

carol_sre: Actionable repro steps I've used to trigger locally: 1) set sticky_ttl to 1s, issue request to primary, wait 2s, send request with same api-key but new session cookie -> observe fallback to fallback region and 401 when auth check hits different auth cluster. 2) Corrupt weights with trailing comma and restart router -> see priority inversion.

alice_support: For now, workaround for customer: set sticky_session: false or increase sticky_ttl to a large value and rotate API keys after we patch. Also we can pin them to dedicated capacity to avoid cross-region auth mismatch.

dave_customer: Ok can you patch soon? The latency and billing spikes are killing our QA runs.

eve_infra: Will roll a hotfix to the config parser to treat malformed weight arrays as validation errors (reject config) and preserve explicit priority semantics. Targeting a canary in 30m. @deploy-bot can you schedule canary?

deploy-bot: deploy requested by eve_infra -> canary group: infra-canaries-1 scheduled at 1912347000. Monitoring hooks: routing-trace, auth-checks, latency. :rocket:

bob_prodeng: Follow-up: add a CI lint rule to reject trailing commas in failover configs and add integration test for sticky_ttl edge cases.

alice_support: I'll send customer an interim mitigation note: disable sticky or bump TTL, and we'll notify when canary is healthy. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

dave_customer: Thanks all — appreciate quick triage. Will hold on changes until you confirm patch.
